messages:
laura: Heads-up — spotted an edge case when migrating from v1 streaming+function-calls to v2. The old shim would interleave tool outputs differently and some clients assume chunk boundaries. Need a short migration note + Node/Python snippet to show recommended framing.

mike: Can you paste an example payload that breaks?

laura: Yep. Repro is: streaming response where tool emits two consecutive tool events with no text between them. v1 shim returned two separate chunks; v2 streaming coalesces into one chunk. Example pseudo: ```json
{"type":"tool","name":"search","output":"hit1"}
{"type":"tool","name":"search","output":"hit2"}
```
Clients expecting chunk-per-tool fail.

ashok: Interesting — runtime coalescing is by design to reduce websocket events. We can add a migration note explaining how to detect tool boundaries from event metadata rather than chunk boundaries.

zara: How urgent is this? Any customers impacted?

laura: One early access customer hit this in their realtime assistant. They can patch client side, but we should update docs and provide code samples.

mike: I can add a small section under "Streaming migration gotchas" + snippets. Suggest two approaches: (1) parse event.type/metadata on the stream to split tool outputs, (2) enable legacy_shim=true (shim toggle) for a short squeeze period if they need exact v1 framing.

jen: I'll write the end-to-end snippet for Node that shows parsing by event.type. Quick draft: ```js
for await (const chunk of resp.stream()) {
  if (chunk.type === 'tool') {
    // accumulate per tool id metadata
  }
}
```
Also add Python snippet for asyncio.

ashok: We should not publicize a long-term legacy_shim flag. If we expose it, mark as "temporary compatibility only" and gate it by account-level flag + warn about cost. Ops can wire it up.

mike: Agreed. Docs PR plan: a small migration note + two snippets + a short alert box recommending parsing by event metadata. Who can review?

laura: I can PR the prose. Jen + Mike review snippets. Ashok for infra wording around shim flag. Zara sign-off for comms.

jen: I can draft Node + Python in a single PR. Will include a tiny test harness.

mike: Also add a tiny unit test in sdk-js repo that shows client parsing of consecutive tool events. That helps docs QA.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy window tomorrow 02:00 UTC for docs site.

laura: TL;DR action items: laura write doc text; jen add Node/Python snippets; mike add unit test and docs links; ashok define wording for temporary shim; zara prepare a short comms blurb for customers. ETA: PRs by EOD Friday.

ashok: Ping me once drafts are up, I'll check the wording for the shim and any telemetry we should attach.

zara: I'll prepare an email/portal note template in case we need to notify impacted customers.

laura: Thanks all — I'll open the PR now and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks — will review.

jen: On it.

laura: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/788 (draft) — added examples and a short migration note. Comments welcome.

mike: Left comments on the Node snippet about edge-case buffering.

jen: Fixed Python snippet per feedback. Pushed a follow-up commit.

ashok: Approving shim wording with the temporary language.

zara: Comms draft ready, linking to PR in portal note.

laura: Merged the docs PR after approvals. Marking this thread resolved.
